team: DE ZERBI: “WE PLAYED VERY, VERY BAD!”  Brentford
quote_text:
Did you ever manage to get kind of  control of the game. Was it fitness,  
not fighting hard enough or too many new players?  For many reasons. I think we are not a team yet,  
for a lot of reasons. Yesterday in the press  conference, when you asked me what is the target?  
The target, we can fix the target when we  become a team. Before we become a team,  
we can’t say what we can do for sure. We are  not at the right point in physical condition,  
for a lot of reasons. The players, they  came late after the World Cup. In Australia,  
we couldn’t work in the right way because of the  trip. We didn’t take risks for a lot of things,  
but they are not excuses. It’s the normal  situation when you are building a new project,  
a new process. I don’t want time, but we have  to pass through these problems. I couldn’t  
lose confidence in my players. I believe in  my players. I believe in my club. I believe  
in myself. I think we are working well. But in  this moment, and I knew after the Hoffenheim game,  
I said we are not at the right point. We are  late for the start of the Premier League. But  
it’s a step we have to improve quickly. Anyway,  we could fight stronger than we did today. We  
lost too many duels. We made too many mistakes  in the timing when we wanted to push the pressure  
higher. We arrived second on the second ball. We  didn’t win one second ball, one duel, one tackle,  
and it’s tough. But if you analyse everything,  you can find that we played with one 2007,  
2006. Lucas Bergvall, the second goal. I think he  didn’t play badly today, even if I substituted him  
at half-time. But Lucas Bergvall, in the next two  seasons, in the next two years, he will not lose  
that ball in that moment of the game. But there  are steps to become better. Now the focus and the  
target is to become a team. You can’t become  a team through the transfer market window,  
through the new players, the players on paper. No,  you become a team with the players when they find  
the connection between them. They find the spirit,  they find the soul. Like I said yesterday, it’s  
a process. Did the depth show today? Do you need  more experience up front in the attacking area?  
No, no, not for the attacking area. For Archie  Gray, the same was [inaudible] today. Like Lucas,  
many new players, maybe they have to  find the connection. Sandro Tonali,  
Senesi and Van Hecke. But I think I don’t change  idea. I think we are working well as a club,  
as a project. We need time, like the big teams  have done in the last 10 years. So, obviously,  
it’s going to take a while for your players to  gel. But given how the team fared towards the  
end of last season, I think a lot of fans will be  shocked by that defeat. Were you shocked? Yeah,  
I’m surprised. I’m suffering for this defeat, but  either we destroy everything or we are working. If  
you analyse last season’s defensive line, Porro,  Danso, Micky van de Ven and Udogie. And today,  
Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Senesi and  Robertson. Four new players. Two midfielders,  
Rodrigo Bentancur, João Palhinha. Today, two  midfielders, Bergvall and [inaudible]. Why not  
Bentancur? Because he came late in pre-season. In  pre-season, we worked with Lucas Bergvall. I think  
at the beginning of the season, at the beginning  of the new project, it was good and it was right  
to play with Lucas Bergvall. But I knew before  the game Lucas Bergvall, in this type of game,  
maybe he could suffer more than Rodrigo Bentancur,  [inaudible] years old, and Lucas 20. I knew before  
the game. But at the end, you have to think  we go and we try to build something good for  
the club. We need also Archie Gray. We need  also Lucas Bergvall, or we work for today and  
tomorrow. I don’t know. For today, I agree with  the plan, with the project, what the club wants  
and the direction we are working. I think it’s  the normal process, even if we are suffering  
for the defeat. And we are shocked by this  defeat, especially for the way we lost the game,  
because they deserved to win and we played very,  very bad. We talked yesterday about keeping the  
balance in terms of excitement levels with  what’s happened this summer. Could this  
match even be quite useful in that regard, for  the players to keep their feet on the ground?  
Yes, but before the game, before this game,  yesterday I told you when you asked me about  
the target, about the happiness for this transfer  market window, I said first of all we have to  
fight to become a team. And to become a team, in  my opinion there are two biggest conditions: the  
soul and the style of play. And today we didn’t  show the soul and we didn’t show the quality of  
play with the ball and without the ball. When  we find these two conditions, I think we can  
become dangerous for everyone, every team. Until  we can’t, until we don’t reach these conditions,  
we have to suffer. And today I think this  defeat is important for us because maybe  
we... Woke up? We [inaudible], maybe. Roberto,  on Archie Gray, the youngest-ever Spurs captain,  
could you provide insight into  the role he will play this season,  
especially with Djed Spence  leaving? Can he play [inaudible]?  
Can play. Archie Gray can play as a full-back, as  a midfielder, but I think he is much better than  
his performance today. But not just Archie  Gray. Also Jan Paul van Hecke, Sandro Tonali,  
Richarlison, everyone. We didn’t play a good  game. Okay, fine. But we can’t change idea  
on Archie Gray for today, or Richarlison,  or Mathys Tel. How long do you expect for  
you to find [inaudible]? Do you expect it to come  before the international break? Do you expect it  
before next week against [inaudible]? We need  time. But I think we are much better than we  
showed today. So from Wednesday we can show our  qualities and we can show who we are. But anyway,  
even if we win Wednesday or next Saturday, we need  time to become a team. Because to become a team,  
we need time. We need time. We have to analyse the  situation. We have to understand the situation,  
the improvement we have to make, every one of us,  because we lose and we win together. Last season,  
obviously, Tottenham were very strong from set  pieces. But losing Romero and [inaudible], two  
key set-piece players for Tottenham last season,  how are you trying to refocus that? Listen,  
Brentford on set pieces are maybe the best team  in the Premier League, so it’s normal to suffer.  
I think we suffered more from the duels, more from  the second ball, than the set pieces. Thank you.
